title: SAE J2716 SENT (Single Edge Nibble Transmission) transmitter and receiver with the slow serial channel (short and enhanced messages)

features: Transmitter: programmable tick (4..4095 PCLK cycles), low time, 1..6 data nibbles, no pause, a fixed pause or constant-length frames
Receiver: synchroniser and glitch filter, calibration pulse within +-25 % sets the tick, ticks rounded from the measured calibration pulse, optional 1/64 drift check
CRC-4 (recommended and legacy) on the fast channel; short (4-bit CRC) and enhanced (6-bit CRC, 8-bit ID / 12-bit data or 4-bit ID / 16-bit data) serial messages both ways
Errors reported one by one: nibble, low time, CRC, pause, missing sync, calibration drift, serial CRC
notes: sent_out is the open-drain style output (1 = released); sent_in is the line as received (it may be sent_out for a loopback).
The receiver holds one frame and one serial message; a frame that arrives while RX is full is dropped and sets RX_OVF.
Not implemented: SPC (short PWM code) master triggers; the fast channel formats (H.1..H.7) are data interpretations left to software.
sequence: Transmit: TX_CFG, TX_PAUSE, TX_FRAME, then CTRL.tx_en; on IRQ TX_FRAME write the next TX_FRAME. Serial: write SER_TX, CMD.ser_tx_start, wait for IRQ SER_TX_DONE.
Receive: RX_CFG and CTRL, IRQ_ENABLE; on IRQ RX_AVAIL read RX0, RX1; on SER_RX_AVAIL read SER_RX; error bits as they come.
